title: Work IQ: federated connectors for governed access to more data sources

reasons: published before the check existed: kept live with a notice while a corrected version is prepared

summary: Hold: the briefing assumes an admin opt-in default and inherited connector controls that Microsoft has not confirmed for this Work IQ change. It also says the roadmap gives no cloud scope despite listing Worldwide, and overstates the absence of automation.

claims.where: front matter: defaultState
claims.claim: Nobody can use Work IQ federated connectors until an administrator opts in.
claims.quote: Searched: Work IQ federated connectors licensing default enabled controls API PowerShell policy; "federated connectors" "Work IQ" "default" "enabled". Opened federated-connectors-overview, manage-federated-connectors, policy-governance-mcp and api-overview; none states this feature's default.
claims.fix: Set defaultState to 'unknown'. State that Microsoft has not stated the arrival default for this roadmap capability; do not infer it from existing connector settings or other Work IQ experiences.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.model and notes; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: Specific licensing for this Work IQ federated-connectors roadmap capability has not yet been published.
claims.quote: Searched: "federated connectors" "Work IQ" licensing availability configuration. Read roadmap, federated-connectors-overview and api-overview; Foundry prerequisites excerpts distinguish API billing from connector licensing but do not specify this roadmap capability's licensing.
claims.fix: Keep licensing.model 'unknown' for this specific roadmap capability, but replace 'Not yet published for Work IQ' with 'Specific licensing for this roadmap capability is not yet published; Work IQ API usage already has published Copilot Credits billing.'

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: Connector-backed tools can have connector-specific licensing requirements for the signed-in user.
claims.quote: Confirm the selected connector's prerequisites. A connector can require a Microsoft 365 Copilot license for each calling user.
claims.fix: Add the Foundry Work IQ page to sources and identify this as background from its preview integration documentation, not a confirmed licensing rule for the new federated-connectors roadmap capability.

claims.where: Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: Work IQ API use can require Copilot Credits billing.
claims.quote: You pay for use of the Work IQ API through a usage-based model that uses Copilot Credits.
claims.fix: Add the Work IQ API overview to sources. Describe the API billing rule as published background, separately from the still-unpublished commercial details of this roadmap capability.

claims.where: front matter: cost; rationale: cost
claims.claim: The identified Work IQ API cost exposure is variable consumption measured in Copilot Credits.
claims.quote: You pay for use of the Work IQ API through a usage-based model that uses Copilot Credits.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Data exposure; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Federated Copilot connectors use MCP to retrieve external data in real time for responses.
claims.quote: Federated connectors use MCP to access data in real time, so Copilot can retrieve up-to-date information directly from external systems.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Security & identity; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Federated connectors access data using the user's identity and permissions.
claims.quote: Access data using the user's identity and permissions.

claims.where: What's changing
claims.claim: Federated connectors do not index external data into Microsoft 365.
claims.quote: Don't index external data into Microsoft 365.

claims.where: What's changing; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: Administrators manage federated connectors in the Microsoft 365 admin center.
claims.quote: Are managed and governed by admins in the Microsoft 365 admin center.

claims.where: Why it matters
claims.claim: Federated connectors do not copy source data into Microsoft 365.
claims.quote: Federated connectors don't copy or store data in Microsoft 365.

claims.where: Why it matters
claims.claim: The source system enforces permissions for federated connector access.
claims.quote: The source system enforces all permissions. Users can only access content they're authorized to view and make changes they're authorized to make in the original data source.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity
claims.claim: Federated connectors use OAuth 2.0.
claims.quote: OAuth 2.0 and encrypted communication ensure secure access and authentication.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Where a connector provides appropriate tools, Copilot can create, update or delete data with user approval.
claims.quote: Can read data and, where a connector provides the tools, create, update, or delete data with the user's approval.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: New write-capable connector tools default to Needs approval.
claims.quote: If a connector publisher adds a new write-capable tool or changes an existing one, the tool is set to Needs approval by default.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support
claims.claim: An MCP server firewall may need static egress IP allow-listing.
claims.quote: If your MCP server restricts incoming traffic by source IP address, configure its firewall to allow the static egress IP addresses used by Microsoft 365 Copilot.

claims.where: What's changing; Open questions: connectors at launch and approval carry-over
claims.claim: Microsoft has not detailed this roadmap capability's launch connector list, presentation or approval carry-over.
claims.quote: Searched: "Work IQ" "federated" "connectors" "governance"; "federated connectors" "Work IQ" licensing availability configuration. Read roadmap, connector overview, Work IQ overview excerpts and API overview; none specifies these launch details.

claims.where: controls[0].ui; Governance controls: first table row
claims.claim: Existing federated connectors can be enabled, disabled or staged under Copilot > Connectors > Your connections.
claims.quote: Enable / Disable | Copilot > Connectors > Your connections | Turns an individual connector on or pauses it without removing configuration. ... Staged rollout | Copilot > Connectors > Your connections > Staged rollout

claims.where: controls[1].ui; Governance controls: second table row
claims.claim: Publisher-type connector availability is controlled at Agents > Settings > Agent and plugin access.
claims.quote: Turn off connectors in bulk by publisher type in Agents > Settings > Agent and plugin access, then turn on specific connectors from Your connections.

claims.where: controls[2].ui; Governance controls: third table row
claims.claim: Agents > Settings > User access controls which users can access plugins, including connectors.
claims.quote: Plugins include tools, MCP servers, connectors, skills, and other AI artifacts. ... Select Agents > Settings > User access to manage your organization's agents and plugins.

claims.where: controls[3].ui; Governance controls: fourth table row
claims.claim: Tenant-level Work IQ MCP policy can be switched on or off at Agents > Tools > Work IQ MCP > Policy.
claims.quote: In the left navigation, select Agents > Tools. ... In the tools registry, select Work IQ MCP. ... On the Work IQ MCP details pane, select the Policy tab when it's available.
claims.fix: Add a note that the Policy tab is available only in tenants with access and appropriate admin permissions; saved policy changes can take up to 24 hours. Keep this as a general Work IQ MCP control unless federated-connector applicability is documented.

claims.where: controls[0].api; Governance controls: first table row
claims.claim: No automation is documented for individual federated connector availability.
claims.quote: Block a Copilot package to prevent its usage. ... POST https://graph.microsoft.com/beta/copilot/admin/catalog/packages/{id}/block
claims.fix: Narrow the null to staged rollout, rather than all availability operations. The package API overview covers MCP servers and plugins; custom-federated-connector guidance says Block has the same effect as Disable. Document POST https://graph.microsoft.com/beta/copilot/admin/catalog/packages/{id}/block and the corresponding /unblock operation for supported connector packages, citing the block/unblock references and noting Microsoft Agent 365 licensing, delegated CopilotPackages.ReadWrite.All and no production support for beta. Do not claim these APIs configure staged rollout.

claims.where: controls[1].api; Governance controls: second table row
claims.claim: An automation equivalent for the publisher-type Agent and plugin access setting is not documented.
claims.quote: Searched: "Agent and plugin access" "User access" "Graph" API settings. Read agent-settings, manage-federated-connectors and Package Management API overview; no publisher-type setting API found.

claims.where: controls[2].api; Governance controls: third table row
claims.claim: An automation equivalent for the tenant-wide User access setting is not documented.
claims.quote: Searched: "Agent and plugin access" "User access" "Graph" API settings. Read agent-settings, manage-federated-connectors and Package Management API overview; no tenant User access setting API found.

claims.where: controls[3].api; Governance controls: fourth table row
claims.claim: An automation equivalent for switching Work IQ MCP tenant policy on or off is not documented.
claims.quote: Searched: Work IQ MCP policy configuration API tenant settings; "Work IQ MCP" "policy" "REST API" settings. Read policy-governance-mcp, API overview and MCP overview excerpts; policy payload concepts are described but no equivalent configuration endpoint or cmdlet is specified.

claims.where: controls[4].ui; controls[4].api; Governance controls: fifth table row
claims.claim: A dedicated Work IQ federated-connectors control is not documented on either admin UI or API surfaces.
claims.quote: Searched: Work IQ federated connectors licensing default enabled controls API PowerShell policy; "Work IQ" "federated" "connectors" "governance". Read roadmap, connector overview, manage-federated-connectors, policy-governance-mcp and API overview; no dedicated control specified.

claims.where: Governance controls: notes and controls[0..3] applicability
claims.claim: Work IQ inherits existing Microsoft 365 Copilot connector enablement and the listed general controls govern this new capability.
claims.quote: Searched: "Work IQ" "federated" "connectors" "governance"; Work IQ federated connectors licensing default enabled controls API PowerShell policy. Read roadmap, connector overview, management and MCP policy pages; none confirms inherited enablement or these controls for this roadmap capability.
claims.fix: Replace 'Work IQ inherits whatever is enabled there' with 'These are existing Copilot connector and Work IQ MCP controls; Microsoft has not confirmed how they apply to this roadmap capability.' Add that qualification to the control notes. Retain the approval carry-over open question; the current definite inheritance claim conflicts with it.

claims.where: Governance controls: notes
claims.claim: Existing federated connector availability settings are located with Microsoft 365 Copilot connector administration.
claims.quote: As an administrator, you manage federated connector availability in the Microsoft 365 admin center.

claims.where: Governance controls: notes
claims.claim: Federated connector governance is portal-only.
claims.quote: A package represents an agent or a tool, such as a plugin, MCP server, or skill, in the organization catalog. ... Block, unblock, and reassign ownership of packages.
claims.fix: Remove 'portal-only'. Say that the listed settings have documented admin-center experiences; beta Package Management APIs can block/unblock supported connector packages, while automation for publisher-type settings, User access and staged rollout was not found. Cite the package overview and block/unblock references without implying blanket API support for all settings.

claims.where: Governance controls: notes; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: Users manage connector write-tool approval settings in Copilot Chat rather than through an administrator approval-setting control.
claims.quote: Users can review or reset tool permissions in Copilot by going to Settings > Sources and selecting the connector. ... Users can also change approval settings for an individual tool.

claims.where: Governance guidance: After rollout; Governance controls: notes
claims.claim: Federated connector activity can be audited in Microsoft Purview.
claims.quote: Can read data and, where a connector provides the tools, create, update, or delete data with the user's approval. Admins can audit activity in Microsoft Purview.

claims.where: Governance guidance: Before rollout and At rollout; Governance controls table
claims.claim: The checklist's connector tool-review and Needs approval controls are represented in the controls table.
claims.quote: Review each connector's write tools. ... Keep write tools on Needs approval. The table contains connector availability, publisher type, User access, Work IQ MCP policy and an undocumented dedicated control, but no tool-permission row.
claims.fix: Add a user-scope row for Copilot Chat > ... > Settings > Sources > connector > Tools > Write/Delete tools, citing the connector overview. Explain that users set Needs approval per tool or group; the admin checklist should communicate this choice rather than imply an enforceable administrator setting.

claims.where: Governance guidance: After rollout; Governance controls table
claims.claim: The checklist's audit control is represented in the controls table.
claims.quote: Audit activity in Microsoft Purview. The controls table has no audit row.
claims.fix: Add a row governing connector activity auditing. The connector overview confirms Purview auditing but does not give a navigation path or automation call; do not invent either. Name the audit capability in the notes until an exact control reference is available.
